## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 — Session relay

### Added (task 1.5.5)
- Added `relay_sessions` and `relay_events` (migration
  `20261022000002_create_relay`). Publication is opt-in per session and off by
  default; a session with no relay row publishes nothing.
- Added `/v1/sessions/{session}/relay` (state, opt in, stop) and
  `/v1/sessions/{session}/relay/events` (publish, backfill). A publish while
  the relay is off, or after it was stopped, is refused; stopping takes effect
  on the next publish because the row is read every time.
- Events carry a per-session monotonic `sequence` and are read with an
  exclusive `after` cursor, so a subscriber that fell behind backfills exactly
  once. Backfill keeps serving what was published after a stop.
- Payloads are a small JSON object (8 KB, depth 3) from a fixed kind list.
  Keys naming credentials or file contents (`token`, `secret`, `env`,
  `password`, `file`, `content`, …) are refused at any depth.
- Documented the contract in `docs/RELAY.md`, including what a relayed event
  may and may not contain.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 — Agent sessions as chat participants

### Added (task 1.5.4)
- A session (a `host_executions` row belonging to one of the organization's
  hosts) can be a room member and a message author. Session principals are
  validated against that table, so an unknown session id cannot join a room or
  post.
- A session message stores the session public id and reads back with the
  project its room belongs to, so a person can talk to an agent and everyone in
  the room can see which agent answered.
- The author principal is serde-tagged `user` or `session`, which is how a
  reader renders a person and an agent differently.
- Session messages outlive the session: the author is a stored id, not a
  foreign key, so ending the execution leaves the history intact.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 — Chatroom live stream and presence

### Added (task 1.5.3)
- Added `GET /v1/chatrooms/{room}/stream?token=<jwt>&after=<sequence>`, a
  WebSocket carrying the same message ids and `sequence` values the HTTP API
  returns. The token travels in the query string because a browser WebSocket
  cannot set an `Authorization` header.
- On connect the socket joins the room hub first, replays history after the
  cursor as `chat.history` frames marked `catchUp: true`, then sends
  `chat.current` once nothing newer exists. A live frame at or below the last
  delivered sequence is dropped, so a reconnecting client sees each message
  exactly once.
- Added `sockets::rooms`: a room-scoped fan-out hub for messages and watcher
  presence. Presence is explicitly not delivery — messages always come from
  the database by cursor, so a stale or missing presence entry can only lose a
  notification, never a message.
- The stream refuses a non-member with the same 404 as a missing room; the
  room list, member list and history are unchanged for HTTP clients.
- Added hub load coverage at the milestone spec: 100 watchers, 1000 messages,
  no drops or double deliveries.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 — Chatroom HTTP API

### Added (task 1.5.2)
- Added `/v1/chatrooms` (rooms the signed-in member belongs to),
  `GET /v1/chatrooms/{room}/members`, `GET /v1/chatrooms/{room}/messages` and
  `POST /v1/chatrooms/{room}/messages`.
- History is cursor-based on the message sequence with `after` and `limit`
  (`1..=200`, default 50). A cursor is exclusive and ordering never depends on
  `created_at`, so paging stays stable while new messages arrive and an empty
  page is the client's currentness signal.
- Membership gates every route. A non-member receives the same 404 as a room
  that does not exist, so private rooms cannot be probed; a viewer may read but
  sending as one is 403.
- Sending validates the body (non-empty, at most 1 MB) before the membership
  check, and both before any insert, so rejected sends write nothing.
- Added unit tests for limit clamping and body/field validation, plus live
  MySQL tests for the 404/403 equivalence, refused writes and paging across
  concurrent inserts.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 — Chatrooms: rooms, members and messages

### Added (task 1.5.1)
- Added `chat_rooms`, `chat_room_members` and `chat_messages` (migration
  `20261022000001_create_chatrooms`). A room belongs to one project, carries a
  name unique within that project, a `private`/`unlisted`/`public` visibility
  and `origin_pool`, which stays `NULL` for every v1 room because federation is
  deferred to v3.
- A member is a pool user or an agent session with an `owner`/`member`/`viewer`
  role and a join time. MySQL refuses a CHECK over a column that also carries a
  foreign-key action, so the one-principal rule is enforced by
  `entities::chatroom::Principal` and by matching unique keys rather than by a
  CHECK constraint.
- Messages carry a stable `public_id`, an author principal, a markdown body and
  an optional reply-to. Ordering is the internal `id`, which MySQL never
  reuses; history reads on `(room_id, id)` and paging uses that id as its
  cursor, so two messages sharing a timestamp cannot be skipped or repeated.
  A deleted author nulls `author_user_id` and the message reads back with no
  author instead of losing its place in history.
- Added `services::chatrooms` with room creation and listing, membership,
  posting and cursor-paged history, all organization-scoped.
- Added a schema test that applies every migration to a throwaway database,
  checks the chatroom tables, indexes and the nullable `origin_pool`, then runs
  the down file and verifies only the chatroom tables disappear; plus a live
  MySQL test for naming conflicts, membership uniqueness, reply addressing and
  stable ordering.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 — Runs, activity log and event receipts

### Added
- Added `event_receipts` (migration `20261021000004_create_activity`): one
  receipt per provider delivery, unique on
  `(organization, provider, connection, delivery key)`. A retry increments
  `duplicate_count` on the existing row, and matching finishes the receipt as
  `matched`, `unmatched` or `rejected` with the run ids it produced.
- Added `agent_conversations`: one row per trigger and thread/issue/pull
  request, holding the agent execution serving it. A later arrival is recorded
  as continuing the conversation, steers it when the agent is busy, or
  restores the conversation when the agent is gone. Reusing a live agent's
  execution is the session relay's job (1.5.5): every arrival still dispatches
  its own executions, so no execution id is shared across runs.
- Added `GET /v1/activity` — cursor-paged history combining receipts, runs,
  steps and executions, filtered by project, provider, trigger, status and
  kind. Every branch is organization-scoped, and filters combine over the
  union so no project's rows can leak into another's page.
- Added `GET /v1/activity/runs/{run}` — the run plus an `arrival` record:
  `created`, `continued` or `restored`, the conversation key, whether it
  steered a busy agent, the receipt, and the output limits that belong to that
  arrival alone.
- Runs now record `provider`, `receipt_public_id`, `conversation_key`,
  `continuation`, `steered` and `output_limits_json`.
  Each arrival keeps its own limits and completion status; a later revision
  cannot rewrite an earlier arrival's snapshot.
- `services::dispatch` now writes a receipt before matching, returns the
  original runs for a duplicate delivery without creating another run, and
  plans continuation per trigger before creating the run.
- Added unit tests for receipt normalization/dedup, conversation grouping,
  continuation steering/restoration, per-arrival output limits and activity
  filter/cursor validation; added ignored MySQL integration tests for filter
  isolation, page shape, receipt dedup and run arrival detail.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-19 — Playzoid becomes Tidepool; TideTable is the plan

Documentation and planning change plus the first implementation task. The plan
is `docs/todo-v1.json`; its rename tasks 1.0.1–1.0.6 carry the rest.

### Pool identity (task 1.1.1)
- Added `organizations` and `pool_users` (migration
  `20261019000001_create_pool_identity`). One organization per pool in v1 is
  enforced by a `UNIQUE` key on a constant `singleton` column; multi-tenancy is
  deferred and recorded in `docs/memory.md`.
- Added first-run setup: `GET /v1/setup/status` and `POST /v1/setup` create the
  organization and owner in the browser, and refuse a second organization.
- Unattended installs bootstrap the first owner from `TIDEBOOT_ORGANIZATION_NAME`,
  `TIDEBOOT_OWNER_EMAIL`, `TIDEBOOT_OWNER_PASSWORD` (at least 12 characters) and
  optional `TIDEBOOT_OWNER_NAME`. The bootstrap is insert-only, so a restart
  never re-applies the temporary password.
- Operators sign in at `POST /v1/pool/login`; `POST /v1/pool/password` replaces
  the bootstrap password and clears `password_change_required`. After the
  change the old password no longer authenticates. Passwords are Argon2id PHC
  strings and the bootstrap secret is never logged (its `Debug` is redacted).
- `GET /v1/pool/me` returns the signed-in operator and organization. Player
  tokens are refused because the subject must resolve to a `pool_users` row.

### Team members, roles and invitations (task 1.1.2)
- Added `pool_invitations` (migration `20261019000002_create_pool_invitations`)
  with single-use, revocable, seven-day tokens. Only an Argon2id hash of the
  token's secret half is stored; the raw token is returned once by
  `POST /v1/pool/invitations`.
- Members accept at `POST /v1/pool/invitations/accept`, choosing their password.
  Replays are refused (409), as are expired and revoked invitations (410).
- Roles are `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. Owners manage the team and
  invitations; viewers are read-only. Every mutating pool handler checks the
  role, so a viewer receives 403.
- The last owner cannot be removed or demoted (409); member mutations lock the
  organization's rows in id order so concurrent owner actions cannot race.
- Removing a member deletes the row, so their existing JWT stops resolving on
  the next request — revocation is immediate.
- Added `OperatorAuth`, which resolves the JWT subject to a `pool_users` row on
  every request; player tokens are refused.

### API keys, scopes and audit (task 1.1.3)
- Added `api_keys` and `audit_events` (migration
  `20261019000003_create_api_keys_and_audit`). Keys are organization-scoped and
  carry explicit scopes: `projects:read`, `configuration:validate`,
  `configuration:install`, `runs:dispatch`, `daemons:enroll`.
- `POST /v1/api-keys` returns the full `<prefix>.<secret>` exactly once; only the
  prefix and an Argon2id hash of the secret are stored. List and whoami return
  the prefix only.
- `GET /v1/api-keys/whoami` authenticates an API key (`X-API-Key` or
  `Authorization: Bearer tpk_...`) and requires `projects:read`. A valid key
  without the scope gets 403; an unknown or revoked key gets 401.
- Revocation (`DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`) sets the key to `revoked`, and
  authentication only selects active rows, so the next request fails
  immediately. Daemon enrollment tokens do not exist yet; when they land their
  issuing key's status must invalidate them.
- Every hub mutation now writes an `audit_events` row with a member, API-key or
  system actor: setup/bootstrap, password change, invitations, role changes,
  member removal, key creation and key revocation.

### Hub API error contract and OpenAPI scopes (task 1.1.4)
- Hub routes (`/v1/setup`, `/v1/pool`, `/v1/api-keys`) now answer failures with
  RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`: `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`,
  `code` and `requestId`. The game API's `{"error": "..."}` bodies are unchanged.
- Added the code taxonomy (`unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `missing_scope`,
  `invalid_request`, `validation_failed`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `gone`,
  `method_not_allowed`, `rate_limited`, `daemon_not_connected`,
  `configuration_invalid`, `service_unavailable`, `internal_error`), documented
  in `docs/HUB_API_ERRORS.md`.
- Added request-id middleware: safe incoming `x-request-id` values are reused,
  otherwise a UUID v4 is generated; the id is echoed on every response and in
  hub problem documents.
- A hub problem middleware is the safety net for extractor failures, unknown
  paths, method mismatches, rate limiting and 5xx responses, so every hub
  failure has the contract shape.
- OpenAPI hub operations now carry `x-auth` (`public` / `member` / `api_key`)
  and `x-required-scope` for API-key routes. New Rust drift tests compare hub
  registrations with the single `ROUTES` table, and the CI scrape validates the
  served extensions.

### Host registry (task 1.2.1)
- Added `hosts` (migration `20261020000001_create_hosts`): immutable public id,
  mutable slug, display name, hostname, status (`pending_approval`,
  `connected`, `offline`, `revoked`) and timestamps.
- `POST /v1/hosts` derives a lowercase kebab-case slug from the hostname and
  de-duplicates with `-2`, `-3`, ...; `PATCH /v1/hosts/{id}` renames the slug or
  display name without changing the id. Explicit collisions return 409.
- `DELETE /v1/hosts/{id}` revokes the relationship from the pool side. Revoked
  hosts are filtered from every endpoint and from dispatch/activation lookups;
  the machine keeps its own local work.
- `services::hosts::resolve_for_activation` fails with a named `host_slug`
  field for an unknown or revoked slug, so configuration activation fails
  before dispatch.

### Host enrollment and relationship credentials (task 1.2.2)
- Added `host_credentials` and `enrollment_tokens` (migration
  `20261020000002_create_host_enrollment`).
- `POST /v1/hosts/enrollment-tokens` mints a ten-minute single-use token bound
  to a registered host. It accepts an API key with `daemons:enroll` or a
  non-viewer member token; the raw token is returned once.
- `POST /v1/hosts/enroll` is the public exchange: the host supplies the token
  and the long-lived credential it generated. Only an Argon2id hash of the
  credential is stored, and no read endpoint returns either secret.
- One host has at most one credential (`UNIQUE host_id`); minting or enrolling a
  host that already has one returns 409. Tokens are single-use and rejected
  after expiry (410) or after the issuing API key is revoked (410).
- `services::enrollment::authenticate_host` verifies the relationship credential
  for later presence and host-protocol work.

### Host presence and heartbeat (task 1.2.3)
- Added an in-memory presence registry and `GET /ws/host`, authenticated with
  the enrollment relationship credential (`X-Host-Id` + `X-Host-Credential`).
  Connect/disconnect moves a host between `connected` and `offline`; the durable
  `hosts.status` projection follows.
- Host sockets send `{"type":"heartbeat"}` and receive
  `{"type":"heartbeat.ack"}`. A missed heartbeat (90s window) marks the host
  offline and closes the socket, even if it is still open.
- Dispatch checks `host_presence::require_connected`: an offline/stale host fails
  immediately with the documented `daemon_not_connected` code instead of being
  queued.
- Added the `tidepool_hosts_connected` gauge and reset leftover `connected`
  rows to offline on process startup. Revoking a host forgets its connections
  and the gauge immediately.

### Host execution grant and capabilities (task 1.2.4)
- Added `hosts.execution_granted` (default false) and `host_capabilities`
  (migration `20261020000003_create_host_capabilities`). Enrollment alone is
  connected-only; `POST /v1/hosts/{id}/execution` makes the separate
  `host.execute` grant and `DELETE` revokes it. `HostView.execution_enabled`
  labels the state.
- With the grant, the host reports providers, models, execution modes, thinking
  options and provider-native option objects at
  `POST /v1/hosts/{id}/capabilities`, authenticated with the relationship
  credential. `GET` returns the report and the offered provider set.
- Only the grantable provider set is offered for pooled execution. Save-time
  validation (`validate_agent_for_host`) names the unavailable
  `provider`, `model`, `execution_mode` or `thinking_option` field instead of
  failing at first dispatch.
- Grant, revoke and report actions are audited.

### Pool host protocol and reference agent (task 1.2.5)
- Added `docs/HOST_PROTOCOL.md`: enrollment, WebSocket authentication,
  heartbeat, capability report, `create_agent`, `execution_started`,
  `execution_output`, `execution_completed`, `interrupt_execution`, errors,
  idempotent replay and reconnect recovery.
- Added `host_executions` (migration `20261020000004_create_host_executions`).
  A stable pool-supplied execution id is the idempotency key; output is
  appended while running and completion records status/output/time. A terminal
  replay returns the existing execution even when the host is offline.
- Added the host protocol service and `/v1/hosts/{id}/executions` to create or
  replay a create-agent intent. Offline dispatch fails with
  `daemon_not_connected`; frames are sent over the host WebSocket.
- Added `crates/tidepool-host-agent`, a minimal blocking reference agent that
  enrolls, reports capabilities, heartbeats, runs one create intent and replays
  completions by execution id. It is excluded from production deployment and
  exists to test the pool without a full host (Swaygent is the suite's host).

### Connection model and provider registry (task 1.3.1)
- Added `connections` and `connection_resources` (migration
  `20261020000005_create_connections`): provider kind, slug, display name,
  credential reference, status and the provider resource identities a
  connection may deliver for.
- Credentials are references to environment/secret-store entries, validated at
  save time and never returned by a read; reads expose only
  `credential_configured`.
- Added the `ConnectionProvider` trait (credential validation, webhook
  verification, resource resolution) and the GitHub/Slack/Discord
  implementations. Adding a provider kind is one implementation plus one
  registry arm.
- `TIDEPOOL_CONNECTIONS` overlays complete environment-defined connections;
  they win on slug, are labelled `managed_by: environment` and cannot be
  mutated through the API.
- Added `/v1/connections` CRUD, documented in `docs/CONNECTIONS.md`.

### GitHub connection and webhooks (task 1.3.2)
- Added `webhook_deliveries` (migration
  `20261020000006_create_webhook_deliveries`) keyed uniquely on
  `(connection_public_id, delivery_id)`.
- `POST /v1/webhooks/github/{slug}` verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` over the raw
  body before matching, records each `X-GitHub-Delivery` once, resolves the
  repository to its connection and maps the documented events to typed internal
  events (`issue.created`, `pull_request.created`, issue/PR comments, review
  comments/reviews, label-added, ping, installation lifecycle).
- Legacy `issue_comment` on a pull request is normalised to
  `pull_request.comment_created`; unknown events are typed `unsupported`.
- `validate_repository` / `resolve_repository_connection` let configuration
  validation refuse an unknown repository with a named `repository` field.
- Documented the App credentials, webhook URL and event mapping in
  `docs/CONNECTIONS.md`.

### Slack connections with socket mode and webhooks (task 1.3.3)
- Added the Slack transport (`src/services/connections/slack.rs`). Both
  transports share normalization, workspace resolution and channel filters:
  `POST /v1/webhooks/slack/{slug}` verifies `X-Slack-Signature` over
  `v0:<timestamp>:<body>` with a five-minute replay window before parsing, and
  socket mode (`SlackSocketSession` + `run_socket_session`) handles Slack's
  envelopes over a frame channel so a pool with no public address needs no
  webhook URL. Slack's `url_verification` handshake is answered with its
  challenge.
- Events are typed `slack.mention` (`app_mention`), `slack.direct_message`,
  `slack.message`, `slack.ignored` (the bot's own posts, subtypes) and
  `slack.unsupported`. A workspace the connection does not own or a filtered
  channel is acknowledged but `accepted: false` with a reason; socket-mode
  envelopes are acknowledged either way so Slack stops retrying.
- Both transports deduplicate on Slack's `event_id` in `webhook_deliveries`
  (`provider = slack`, transport in `action`), so a retry — or the same event
  arriving on both transports — is recorded once. Socket-mode sessions also
  dedup in memory across a reconnect.
- The bot mention is stripped before the text is exposed: a normalized message
  carries prompt-safe `text` plus `raw_text` for the record.
- Added the declared-output registry (`src/services/outputs.rs`) with
  `slack.reply`. `OutputLedger` refuses an undeclared capability, enforces
  `maximum` (default 1, hard maximum 20) and fails `finish()` when a `required`
  capability was never emitted, so a step that must answer cannot complete
  silently. A reply is constructed from its event, so it can only land in the
  channel and thread the event came from.
- `validate_workspace` / `resolve_workspace_connection` let configuration
  validation refuse an unknown workspace with a named `workspace` field.
- Documented credentials, both transports, the event table and the reply
  capability in `docs/CONNECTIONS.md`.

### Discord connections over the bot gateway (task 1.3.4)
- Added the Discord transport (`src/services/connections/discord.rs`). Discord
  has no inbound webhook for bot events, so there is no route: the pool dials
  the gateway WebSocket and `DiscordGatewaySession` owns the protocol — hello,
  identify or resume, heartbeat, dispatch, `op 7`/`op 9` — while
  `run_gateway_session` pumps it over a frame channel, so a live socket and a
  scripted test feed drive identical logic.
- Events are typed `discord.mention` (a guild message mentioning the bot),
  `discord.direct_message`, `discord.message`, `discord.ignored` (the bot's own
  and other bots' posts, webhook posts, `MESSAGE_UPDATE`) and
  `discord.unsupported`. A guild the connection does not own or a filtered
  channel is handed on but `accepted: false` with a reason.
- **A reconnect does not duplicate an event.** The session's dedup window (the
  last 1024 message snowflakes) lives on the session rather than on the socket,
  so it survives the redial that caused the replay and a resumed stream's
  replayed events are handed on once. `webhook_deliveries` (`provider =
  discord`, `gateway`/`gateway_resume` in `action`) backstops that window across
  a restart.
- The bot mention is stripped before the content is exposed: `<@id>` and the
  nickname form `<@!id>` go, role mentions stay, and a normalized message
  carries prompt-safe `content` plus `raw_content` for the record. `READY`
  supplies the bot user id when credentials did not.
- Added `discord.reply` to the output registry with the same semantics as
  `slack.reply` (default `maximum` 1, hard maximum 20, optional `required`),
  enforced by the same `OutputLedger`. A reply is built from its event, so it
  lands in the originating channel — or the thread, which in Discord *is* the
  channel — with `allowed_mentions: {"parse": []}` so no agent output can ping
  anyone.
- `validate_guild` / `validate_guilds_for_activation` fail activation with a
  named `guild` field when the organization has no active connection for a
  guild, so a trigger that could never fire is refused at save time.
- The session never holds the bot token: frames that need it name the
  credential field and the value is injected at send time, which stays with
  dispatch (task 1.4.6) along with dialling the socket and the reply call.
- Documented the handshake, the resume/dedup rule, the event table and the
  reply capability in `docs/CONNECTIONS.md`.

### Project model and configuration revisions (task 1.4.1)
- Added `projects`, `configuration_revisions` and `configuration_revision_files`
  (migration `20261021000001_create_projects`). A project is `slug` + `name`,
  scoped to the organization. A revision is an immutable authored file set
  (path + raw content, stored verbatim), a per-project `version`, an `active`
  flag and the validation result; rows are write-once and only `active` ever
  changes.
- Added `GET/POST /v1/projects` and `GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/projects/{id}`.
  Project reads accept a member or a `projects:read` key; mutations require a
  non-viewer member (there is no project-write key scope).
- Added `POST /v1/projects/{id}/configuration/validate`
  (`configuration:validate`) — a dry run that resolves every reference and
  writes nothing — and `POST /v1/projects/{id}/configuration/install`
  (`configuration:install`), which always stores a new revision and either
  activates it or, on failure, records the issue and leaves the previous
  active revision in place.
- Validation resolves every reference in the bundle: connection slugs (active
  connection), host slugs (live host), environments (named, each referencing a
  host), named agents (well-formed) and prompt partials (referencing a file in
  the bundle). Every unresolvable reference is reported as a
  `{ field, revision, message }` issue naming both the field and the revision.
- `GET /v1/projects/{id}/configuration` returns the active revision and
  `GET /v1/projects/{id}/revisions[/{revision_id}]` the history. The manifest
  is `tidepool.json`; the authored files are stored exactly, never normalized.

### Trigger schema and validation endpoint (task 1.4.2)
- Added the trigger document: the provider `event` it listens for
  (`{ provider, type }`), its `filters`, and the `run` it starts
  (`{ host, agent }`, where `agent` is a `provider`/`model`/`execution_mode`/
  `thinking_option` selection).
- `filters` is required and `from_users` must be present and non-empty. The
  allowlist is the one layer that keeps a stranger's comment on a public issue
  from starting an agent on someone's machine, so a missing or empty allowlist
  is a hard rejection, never a default.
- Filters cover the provider resource (`resource.kind` + `resource.id`), the
  connection (`connection` slug), the invoking user (`from_users`), a
  `channel` or `label`, and a `contains` or `pattern` guard. Every condition is
  a conjunction — all must pass, and there is no "any" mode.
- Added `POST /v1/triggers/validate` (`configuration:validate`, or a
  non-viewer member). It compiles one document, resolves the connection,
  resource and host, and asks the named host whether it can run the agent,
  returning `{ name, valid, errors }` without writing pool state. Unknown
  connection/resource/host and an agent the host cannot run are each reported
  as a named `{ field, message }` issue.

### Environment model (task 1.4.5)
- Added `Environment` (`src/entities/environment.rs`): a complete named object
  with an enrolled host slug, an absolute working directory on that machine and
  an optional worktree. The pool never clones, creates or rewrites the
  directory. `deny_unknown_fields` means an `extends`/overlay key is a parse
  error, so two environments can never be merged or partially overridden.
- Worktrees carry a mode (`branch-off` or `checkout-branch`), a new branch
  template and an optional base ref. `branch-off` renders
  `${{ paseo.execution.id }}` (or `${{ tidepool.execution.id }}`) into the
  branch, so every execution gets its own branch; any other expression, a
  missing execution id, an unsafe execution id or an invalid rendered Git ref
  fails activation. `checkout-branch` takes a literal branch only.
- Configuration activation (`tidepool.json` `environments`) now runs the full
  environment resolver: an unknown host, a missing/relative/non-canonical
  directory, a duplicate name and a bad worktree each name their authored field
  (`environments.<name>.<field>`) and keep the previous revision active.
  `configuration::parse_environments` returns the authored definitions for
  dispatch (task 1.4.6) unchanged.
- Added the finite selector: a step names one environment literally or through
  a finite input whose every declared choice must resolve at activation. A
  selector resolves to exactly one complete environment.
- Added dispatch resolution (`src/services/environments.rs`): the pure
  `resolve_dispatch` picks the environment, requires its host and renders the
  per-execution branch; the database wrapper asks presence. An offline host
  fails with `daemon_not_connected` and nothing is queued.

### Workflow schema (task 1.4.4)
- Added `Workflow` (`src/entities/workflow.rs`): one trigger name and an
  ordered list of steps. A step carries a unique id, an environment selector, a
  named or complete static inline agent, an ordered prompt of text and partial
  includes, an optional condition over declared inputs and earlier step output,
  an optional finite output schema, its declared output capabilities, and its
  own maximum runtime and idle timeout.
- Steps run in authored order. A `reads` entry, a condition operand and a
  `${{ steps.<id>... }}` prompt expression may reference only an earlier step;
  a later step or the step itself is rejected. Step ids are unique and stable
  (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`).
- An agent is either a named agent or one complete static inline
  configuration. A dynamic inline object is parsed so validation can name it
  and is then refused; an inline field carrying an expression is refused too.
- Added `src/services/workflows.rs`, which validates workflows against the
  revision's environments, named agents and prompt partials and reports a
  named `{ field, message }` issue for every failure. Output capabilities are
  checked through the existing `OutputLedger` registry.
- A finite output property (`enum` or `const`) may bound a later input choice:
  every declared choice must be in the finite set. An unbounded property does
  not constrain the choice. `finite_choice_bounds` exposes the resulting bound
  for dispatch.
- Deadlines compose: the workflow maximum runtime is the outer bound, and the
  remaining time caps both a step's maximum runtime and its idle timeout
  (`Workflow::effective_deadlines`).
- Configuration activation now validates the `workflows` array in
  `tidepool.json` and adds `configuration::parse_workflows` for dispatch. The
  bundle caps are enforced with the failing path named: at most 100 files, a
  512-character path, 1,000,000 characters per file and 5,000,000 bytes of
  referenced prompt partials. Paths must be relative and canonical; unsafe,
  duplicate and extra (unreferenced) files are rejected.
- Added unit tests per rule and per cap plus an ignored live-MySQL integration
  test that installs a two-step, one-partial workflow.

### Trigger installation and revisions (task 1.4.3)
- Added `triggers` and `trigger_revisions` (migration
  `20261021000002_create_triggers`). A trigger belongs to one project and its
  name is unique per project (`(project_id, name)`), so two projects may each
  own an `auto-fix-issues`. A revision is write-once: it carries a per-trigger
  `version`, an `active` flag and the exact installed document as JSON.
- Added `POST /v1/triggers/install` (`configuration:install`, or a non-viewer
  member). It validates the document with the same resolver validate uses and
  then creates or replaces the project's trigger of that name, returning
  `{ id, name, revision, version, active, replaced }`.
- A first install creates the trigger at version 1. A second install of the
  same name keeps the trigger's `public_id` (its identity, so the history stays
  one readable history), appends a new revision and deactivates the previous
  one. Old revisions are never renumbered or deleted.
- An invalid document writes nothing at all: no trigger row, no revision, no
  deactivation, no audit entry. The failure is a 422 `configuration_invalid`
  naming every failing field, so a later failure never undoes an earlier
  success. A missing project is a 404.
- The install body is the trigger document plus one `project` key, parsed so
  `deny_unknown_fields` still applies; a missing or unusable `project` is a 400.
- Added unit tests for create-then-replace, revision numbering (including a
  version gap), identity retention, the invalid-document rule and
  install-after-failure, plus ignored live-MySQL integration tests for the
  create/replace cycle, partial failure across two installs, an unknown project
  and per-project name uniqueness.

### Dispatch and run lifecycle (task 1.4.6)
- Added `runs` and `run_steps` (migration `20261021000003_create_runs`). A run
  snapshots the dispatch-time workflow, environments and prompt partials, so a
  restart evaluates exactly what was dispatched. The delivery key is unique per
  trigger: an event retry or a manual resubmission returns the existing run.
- Added `POST /v1/runs` (`runs:dispatch`, or a non-viewer member) for manual
  dispatch: `{ project, trigger, actor, revision?, deliveryKey, input }`.
  Leading `key=value` tokens fill declared inputs and the first non-assignment
  token starts the request text. The actor must be in the trigger's
  `from_users`; an expected revision that is no longer active is a 409. A new
  run is 201; a key that already names one is 200 with `deduplicated: true` —
  deduplication is promised, exactly-once delivery is not.
- Added event dispatch (`services::dispatch::dispatch_event`): every active
  trigger whose event, connection, resource, actor, channel, label, `contains`
  and `pattern` filters all pass starts one run; `*`/`?` are the pattern's only
  metacharacters.
- Dispatch resolves every step's environment before inserting anything. An
  offline host therefore fails with `daemon_not_connected` and writes no run or
  step row — nothing is queued.
- Added the run lifecycle (`services::runs`): one step at a time, conditions
  skip a step without failing the run, and the workflow/step deadlines cap each
  step. A passed deadline fails the run and skips every later step. Conditions
  read declared inputs and earlier step outputs; prompts render `inputs.*`,
  `request`, `steps.<id>` and `steps.<id>.<property>`.
- Create-intent idempotency: the execution id is derived deterministically from
  the run's public id and step id, stored before the frame is sent. A lost
  response, host reconnect or pool restart re-sends the same id; the host
  answers with the existing execution. A succeeded execution is recorded from
  the ledger; a failed or interrupted one becomes `interrupted` and is never
  started again.
- Wired completion into the host socket and recovery into startup and host
  reconnect (files outside the task's owned paths), so observed completions
  advance the run and a reconnected host replays its pending intents.
- Added unit tests for input parsing, filter matching, glob patterns,
  condition evaluation, prompt rendering, deadline arithmetic, execution-id
  determinism and the create decision, plus ignored live-MySQL integration
  tests for event/manual dispatch, offline dispatch, restart replay and
  condition/deadline outcomes.

### Fixed
- Docker builds copy the workspace's `crates/` directory and build only the
  `tidepool` package, so the reference host-agent member no longer breaks the
  image build.

### Changed
- **Product name: Playzoid → Tidepool.** The suite's design system
  (`clawffice-design`) had already assigned this product the name Tidepool (hub
  and game server, hue `tide`). The repository becomes `ClawfficeOrg/Tidepool`,
  the crate and binary `tidepool`, and the Prometheus prefix `tidepool_*`.
  Renaming the metric prefix is a **breaking change** for anyone scraping
  `/metrics`: `playzoid_http_requests_total`,
  `playzoid_http_request_duration_seconds`, `playzoid_ws_connections` and
  `playzoid_db_pool_connections` become `tidepool_*`. GitHub keeps a redirect
  from the old repository name. The game API surface does not change.
- **The plan is now TideTable JSON.** `docs/todo-v1.json` (v1, ships `0.5.0`)
  is the rename and the hub; `docs/todo-v2.json` (v2, ships `0.6.0`) is the
  clients (contract, TypeScript/Rust/Python SDKs, CLI, Svelte control plane,
  ratatui console, Zoid reference client). Task ids, the `task/vX.Y.Z` branch
  pattern and the CI-green merge gate are unchanged.
- `docs/todo-v0.md` and `docs/todo-v1.md` are **frozen** as the record of
  releases 0.1–0.4 and take no new tasks; `docs/todo.md` is now the index and
  points at the TideTable files.

### Added
- `docs/todo-v1.json` — TideTable v1 plan (rename, pool identity, hosts,
  connections, triggers/workflows/dispatch, chatrooms + session relay,
  self-hosting).
- `docs/todo-v2.json` — TideTable v2 plan (the client surfaces above).
- `docs/HUB_CAPABILITIES.md` — Paseo Hub read and mapped to Tidepool capability
  by capability. Read for product shape only: no Paseo code, schema,
  configuration format, database or wire protocol is copied or ported.

### Notes
- Cross-file prerequisites do not validate in TideTable, so `docs/todo-v2.json`
  records its v1 dependencies in a `requires_v1` field (documented under
  `meta.cross_file_dependencies`). A supervisor must not start a v2 task while
  those entries are pending.

### Crate, binary and Prometheus namespace (task 1.0.2)
- The Cargo package is `tidepool`, so the binary is `target/{debug,release}/tidepool`
  and the Docker entrypoint is `/app/tidepool`. `use playzoid_server::…` in
  `src/` and `tests/` becomes `use tidepool::…`, and the CI OpenAPI job boots
  `./target/debug/tidepool`.
- **Breaking for scrapers:** the Prometheus prefix is now `tidepool_`. The four
  series rename with no compatibility aliases:

  | Old | New |
  |---|---|
  | `playzoid_http_requests_total` | `tidepool_http_requests_total` |
  | `playzoid_http_request_duration_seconds` | `tidepool_http_request_duration_seconds` |
  | `playzoid_ws_connections` | `tidepool_ws_connections` |
  | `playzoid_db_pool_connections` | `tidepool_db_pool_connections` |

  Dashboards, alerts and recording rules matching the old names must be updated.
  The HTTP API surface is unchanged.

### Dev stack, CI and deploy identifiers (task 1.0.3)
- `config/docker-compose.dev.yml`: database `playzoid_dev` → `tidepool_dev`, user
  `playzoid` → `tidepool`, and the server's `DATABASE_URL` follows.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the sqlx job's `MYSQL_DATABASE` and
  `DATABASE_URL` use `tidepool`, and the Docker smoke image tag is `tidepool:ci`.
- `.env.example` uses the new database URL and `RUST_LOG=…,tidepool=debug`.
- Migration files are **not** rewritten — they are forward-only and already
  applied. `docs/README.md` documents how to carry an existing `playzoid_dev`
  volume over to `tidepool_dev` without losing data.

### Docs, branding and the game-API guard (task 1.0.5)
- New root `README.md`: Tidepool's role (hub and game server, self-hostable,
  open), the clawffice-design identity (tide hue, water current, rock-pool
  creature), quick start, endpoints, metrics prefix and repository layout.
  Design tokens are referenced from `clawffice-design`, not vendored.
- `docs/README.md`, `docs/GUIDELINES.md`, `docs/TALO_API.md` and
  `skills/ralph.md` no longer call the current project by its former name;
  historical records (`CHANGES.md`, `memory.md`, `RECOVERY_PLAN.md`, the frozen
  todo files, `ralph-log.md`, `learnings.md`) keep the old name where they

- OpenAPI gains `game_routes_are_unmoved_under_v1`: the table must still hold
  22 route specs, 19 of them under `/v1/`, with only `/healthz`, `/metrics` and

### TideTable task loop (task 1.0.6)
- `skills/ralph.md` drives the TideTable plan: `validate`, `ready --disjoint`,
  `next`, `start` to claim under a lease, `look-defer` when the PR opens and
  `look-clear` after merge. It no longer parses markdown task lines, and the

- `docs/GUIDELINES.md` PR and release steps reference task ids in the TideTable

## [0.4.1] — 2026-10-12 — security bump, CI restart, bounded startup

Patch release on top of `0.4.0`, tagged `v0.4.1`. Covers the fixes found while
reviewing the Phase 0.4 release PR (#21); `v0.4.0` remains the phase-completion
marker. No API or schema changes.

### Fixed
- `cargo audit` is clean again after four advisories landed against `rustls`
  0.23.45 on 2026-10-14. Lockfile-only update: `rustls` 0.23.45 → 0.23.46,
  which clears **RUSTSEC-2026-0346** (`Debug` impls expose TLS secrets,
  medium), **RUSTSEC-2026-0347** (buffered data sent after ECH rejection, low),
  **RUSTSEC-2026-0348** (Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to
  1 GiB, low) and **RUSTSEC-2026-0349** (ServerHello can downgrade to classical
  key exchange, low). Reached via `sqlx-core` → `sqlx-mysql`; no `Cargo.toml`
  change required and no other versions moved.
- `cargo audit` is clean again after the advisory database advanced past the
  last dependency bump. Lockfile-only update: `rustls` 0.23.40 → 0.23.45
  (plus `rustls-webpki` 0.103.13 → 0.103.15), which clears
  **RUSTSEC-2026-0285** (TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted
  across encryption-level boundaries, medium, fixed in `>=0.23.45`).
  Reached via `sqlx-sqlite` → `sqlx-core`; no `Cargo.toml` change required
  and no other versions moved. The four remaining advisories are
  non-gating warnings with documented policy (`anyhow`,
  `event-listener`, `chacha20`, `spin`).
- **Startup hung forever when Redis was unreachable.** Re-enabling CI exposed a
  failing `openapi` job: the process stayed alive but never bound a socket, so
  `/openapi.json` was never served. `redis::aio::ConnectionManager::new` has no
  default connect timeout and its retry loop re-arms indefinitely, and `main`
  awaited it after the DB pool — so the "degraded mode" path never ran and
  `HttpServer::bind` was never reached. New `src/services/redis.rs` wraps the
  handshake in a 3s timeout and returns a plain error for the caller to
  warn-log, mirroring `db::build_pool`'s explicit `acquire_timeout`. Startup is
  now bounded (≈5s MySQL + 3s Redis worst case) and boots degraded as designed.

### CI
- Re-enabled CI triggers. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` had drifted to
  `workflow_dispatch`-only, so no workflow ran on pull requests and GitHub
  reported "no checks reported"; the `AGENTS.md` "CI green" merge gate was
  unsatisfiable. Now runs on pushes to `main` and `release/**` and on pull
  requests targeting `main`. `workflow_dispatch` retained for manual re-runs.

### Docs
- Corrected the RC-tag rule in `docs/todo-v1.md`: it claimed *this* line
  (`0.4`) has `Y = 0`, but the release line is `0.4`, so `Y = 4`. The rule
  itself is unchanged and now matches `docs/todo-v0.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-12 — governance repairs + `.env` security incident

Follow-ups on top of `v0.4.1`; not covered by that tag.

### Security
- **`.env` removed from tracking.** It was committed in `a778497` and had been
  present in every branch and all four tags since, exposing a real `JWT_SECRET`
  in a **public** repository. `git rm --cached .env` plus `.gitignore` rules
  (`.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`) prevent re-committing. The key must be
  treated as compromised and rotated regardless — removal from history does not
  un-leak a published value. `.env.example` now documents per-environment
  generation (`openssl rand -hex 64`).
- Enabled GitHub **secret scanning** and **push protection** on the repository
  (secret scanning had been disabled, which is why this went unnoticed).
- Follow-up: purge `.env` from history (`git filter-repo`) and force-push all
  refs + re-create tags. Requires temporarily relaxing `TagProtect`.

**Done:** history rewritten (`git filter-repo --path .env --invert-paths`); all
11 branches force-pushed, all 4 tags deleted and recreated; `release/v0.4` tree
hash byte-identical so prior validation still holds; local clone re-synced.
`TagProtect` disabled only for the tag delete/recreate, then restored.

**⚠️ Residual:** GitHub's `refs/pull/{14..20}/head` still pin the original
pre-rewrite commits, so `.env` remains retrievable from the remote despite the
rewrite. Hidden refs cannot be deleted by git or API (`deny updating a hidden
ref`) — a GitHub Support request to GC unreachable objects is required. Mitigated
by rotation: the key is useless. **Never assume a history rewrite alone
remediates a leaked secret.**

### Repository governance
- **`MainProtect` ruleset repaired.** It was named for `main` but matched
  `~ALL` (`ref_name.include: ["~ALL"]`) while carrying both the `update` and
  `creation` rules — so, minus bypass actors, *no one* could push to or create
  *any* branch. Now scoped to `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` and given real teeth:
  `pull_request` (1 approval, stale-review dismissal, thread resolution) and
  `required_status_checks` (`Lint & Test`, `cargo-audit`, `OpenAPI drift
  check`, `sqlx migrate (mysql)`). Bypass actors trimmed 6 → 1 (Organization
  admin only), down from generic org/deploy-key/repo-role/team entries that
  made the ruleset decorative.
- **New `ReleaseBranchProtect` ruleset** — `deletion` + `non_fast_forward` for
  `refs/heads/release/**`, restoring force-push protection that the re-scoping
  would otherwise have removed.
- **New `TagProtect` ruleset** — `deletion` + `update` for `refs/tags/v*`, so
  release tags cannot be silently re-pointed or removed.


### Fixed
- **Startup hung forever when Redis was unreachable.** Re-enabling CI exposed a
  failing `openapi` job: the process stayed alive but never bound a socket, so
  `/openapi.json` was never served. `redis::aio::ConnectionManager::new` has no
  default connect timeout and its retry loop re-arms indefinitely, and `main`
  awaited it after the DB pool — so the "degraded mode" path never ran and
  `HttpServer::bind` was never reached. New `src/services/redis.rs` wraps the
  handshake in a 3s timeout and returns a plain error for the caller to
  warn-log, mirroring `db::build_pool`'s explicit `acquire_timeout`. Startup is
  now bounded (≈5s MySQL + 3s Redis worst case) and boots degraded as designed.

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-26 — Redis-backed rate limiting (task 0.4.8)

### Added
- Fixed-window rate limiting on public routes (`src/middleware/rate_limit.rs`): one Redis bucket per `(class, client ip, window_start)` key, incremented by an atomic `EVAL` `INCR`+`EXPIRE`+`TTL` script so limits hold across workers/instances. Registered globally; enforcement scoped internally to configured public prefixes (`/v1/auth`, `/auth`, `/ws` by default; `/healthz` never limited).
- Two budgets: `auth` (credential endpoints, tight — brute-force backstop) and `default` (other public routes). Config via `RATE_LIMIT_*` env (see `src/config.rs`), validated at startup; `RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_XFF` opts into `X-Forwarded-For` client identification (opt-in only — header is spoofable without an overwriting proxy).
- Blocked requests answer `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` + `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset` headers and the standard `{"error": ...}` JSON body. Response is built from the consumed `ServiceRequest` — the inner `HttpRequest` is never cloned, because actix panics when downstream calls `match_info_mut()` on an `Rc` whose refcount is > 1.
- Degraded mode is fail-open by design (availability over strictness, `docs/memory.md`): Redis down at boot → no limiter app data → pass-through; mid-flight backend error → allow + warn-log.
- Architecture: middleware future is `'static`, so the inner service is stored as `Arc<S>` (needs `S: 'static`, not `S: Clone`); `RateLimiter` is a single concrete type over `Arc<dyn WindowCounter>` (object-safe `CounterFuture`) so `app_data` lookups always match; an injectable `NowFn` clock makes fixed-window rollover deterministic in tests.
- Unit tests same-file (24): key/classification/decision math, deplete-then-429, budget holds until `Retry-After - 1`, window resets after elapse, fail-open paths, degraded pass-through, excluded paths never hit the backend.

### Security note
- Auth-class budgets slow credential brute-force; per-IP buckets keyed on socket peer by default.

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-26 — player feedback endpoint (task 0.4.7)

### Added
- `POST /v1/feedback` — auth-gated player feedback submission. Body `{ "message": <text> }` with unknown fields rejected; trimmed message must be 1..=1000 chars (`MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS`, socket-chat gate precedent) and its JSON-encoded payload ≤ 4 KiB (`MAX_PROPS_BYTES`, events precedent — escape-heavy control-char input can trip the encoded cap while remaining length-valid). Stored verbatim after trimming.
- Storage reuses the append-only `analytics_events` table (task 0.4.5): one row per submission with `name = "feedback"` and `props = { "message": ... }` — no new migration; a dedicated table stays a Phase 1.0 candidate (recorded in `docs/memory.md`).
- Honest-failure contract (deliberate divergence from fire-and-forget events): a post-validation database failure answers `500 {"error": "internal error"}` with details logged server-side only — user content must never be silently dropped. Success: `201 Created {"received": true}`.
- Best-effort attribution: unknown/deleted callers (or a failing resolution query) store anonymous rows (`player_id NULL`) rather than failing — account state never loses feedback text.
- `src/services/feedback.rs` — `submit_feedback`, pure pre-SQL `validate`, `FeedbackServiceError` (`Invalid`/`Database`); static `.bind()`-only INSERT into `analytics_events`.
- `src/api/feedback.rs` — single canonical `/v1/feedback` route (no legacy alias, post-0.4.1 precedent); guard order cheapest-first (auth 401 → pool 503 → validation 400 → insert).
- Unit tests same-file (API 10 + service 7) + `tests/feedback_integration.rs` (5 `#[ignore]`d live-stack tests incl. deleted-player anonymous storage and writes-nothing-on-reject).
- Wired into `src/{api,services}/mod.rs` and `src/main.rs`.

### Security note
- Authenticated-only submission; length + encoded-size caps bound per-request abuse until rate limiting lands (task 0.4.8).

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-26 — analytics events ingest endpoint (task 0.4.6)

### Added
- `POST /v1/events` — auth-gated batched analytics-event ingest (fire-and-forget). Body is a bare JSON array `[{"name", "props"?}, ...]` validated whole-batch before any SQL: non-empty, ≤100 events (`MAX_BATCH_EVENTS`), trimmed `name` 1..=64 chars matching `VARCHAR(64)`, serialized `props` ≤ 4 KiB mirroring the leaderboards cap; unknown per-event fields rejected at deserialization; no client timestamps (`created_at` DB-stamped, append-only).
- Fire-and-forget contract: accepted batches answer `202 Accepted {"accepted": n}` after one batched multi-row INSERT; any post-validation database failure is logged (`tracing::error!`) but still answered 202 — telemetry loss must never block clients. Pool absent → 503 (degraded-mode precedent).
- Best-effort player attribution: JWT identity resolves to the internal `players.id`; unknown/deleted callers store anonymous rows (`player_id NULL`) rather than failing — account state never breaks intake.
- `src/entities/analytics_event.rs` — `AnalyticsEventRow` insert-shape struct; deliberately no `FromRow`/View (the table is write-only in v0 and never selected).
- `src/services/events.rs` — `ingest_events` + pure pre-SQL `validate_batch`, `MAX_BATCH_EVENTS`/`MAX_EVENT_NAME_LEN`/`MAX_PROPS_BYTES` caps, `EventsServiceError` (`Invalid`/`Database`). Batched INSERT uses `sqlx::QueryBuilder::push_values` — placeholder scaffolding only, every value bound.
- `src/api/events.rs` — single canonical `/v1/events` route (no legacy alias, post-0.4.1 precedent); guard order cheapest-first (auth 401 → pool 503 → validation 400 → insert).
- Unit tests (entity/service/API same-file, incl. dead-DB-still-202 proof) + `tests/events_integration.rs` (10 `#[ignore]`d live-stack tests: attribution, batch atomicity, NULL props, exact-limit boundary, deleted-player anonymization).
- Wired into `src/{api,services,entities}/mod.rs` and `src/main.rs`.

### Security note
- Authenticated-only ingest; per-request cost bounded by caps (~400 KiB worst case) until rate limiting lands (task 0.4.8).

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-26 — analytics events schema (task 0.4.5)

### Added
- `migrations/20260826000002_create_analytics_events.up.sql` — `analytics_events` append-only event log: auto-increment internal id, nullable `player_id` FK to `players` with **ON DELETE SET NULL** (deleting a player must never erase their events — CASCADE would break append-only semantics), free-form `name VARCHAR(64)` event key, optional JSON `props` payload, `created_at`. No `updated_at` and no `public_id`: rows are never updated and clients never address a stored event (write-only ingest in v0). Schema stays deliberately generic (`name` + JSON) — typed event schema is an open question deferred to Phase 1.0; upstream Talo's event shape is undocumented in this repo so no upstream-specific columns were guessed. `props` size cap is enforced at the API layer (task 0.4.6); MySQL JSON columns cannot be size-bounded in schema. Indexes kept minimal for a high-write log: `(player_id)` and `(name, created_at)`.
- `migrations/20260826000002_create_analytics_events.down.sql` — reversible drop.
- `docs/todo-v1.md` — task 0.4.5 marked done with done-note.

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-26 — per-game settings endpoints (task 0.4.4)

### Added
- `GET /v1/games/{game_id}/settings` — auth-gated read of one game's stored JSON config; unknown game → 404. No legacy alias mount (route created after the 0.4.1 prefix-parity pass; `/v1/socket-tickets` precedent).

- `src/api/game_settings.rs` — handlers + single canonical `/v1/games` scope; body wrapper `{ "config": <any> }` rejects unknown top-level fields while keeping the inner config arbitrary JSON. Error mapping: invalid → 400, unknown → 404, pool absent → 503.

### Added
- `src/entities/prop.rs` — shared `Prop { key, value }` pair used across every upstream entity.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-08-25 — WebSocket subaccount participant support (task 0.3.14)

### Changed
- `src/sockets/channels.rs` — the channel hub's membership registry is rekeyed to **participant groups**: `channel → group → alias → conn_key → Recipient`, with the reverse index widened to `conn_key → (channel, group, alias)`. A channel's participants are its distinct groups (server-resolved `parent_account_id`, or the alias itself for roots), so the first connection of a group announces `v1.channels.player-joined` (carrying the joining alias), the last connection announces `v1.channels.player-left` (carrying the departing alias), and chat fans out to every connection across the channel's participant groups — a subaccount and its parent share membership and each other's chat. `JoinChannel`/`LeaveChannel` carry the alias's resolved `parent_account_id` (the hub derives the group); `ChannelMessage` carries a server-stamped `group` and the send gate is group-level membership. `LeaveAllChannels` now keys on `conn_key` only (the reverse index already knows each membership's channel/group/alias). Envelopes stay Talo-verified and per-alias — grouping is visible only in membership sharing.
- `src/sockets/ws.rs` — `WsConn` gains the server-resolved `parent_account_id` and `ws_index` gains an `Option<web::Data<MySqlPool>>` extractor that resolves it best-effort on connect (missing pool / unknown alias / lookup error degrade to `None`, never failing the connection). `FrameOutcome::JoinChannel` carries the parent; the message handler stamps the sender's group from the ticketed alias + resolved parent (spoof-proof). The `v1.players.identify.success` data gains an **additive** `parentAccountId` (null for roots / degraded DB).
- `src/sockets/groups.rs` (new) — `resolve_parent_account_id` (parameterized `SELECT parent_account_id … WHERE status <> 'deleted'`), pure `group_key`, and `resolve_group`.

### Added
- Hub unit tests: group-level join idempotency (subaccount joins parent's group silently), subaccount ↔ parent chat sharing (both directions, per-conn single delivery), distinct parents as distinct participants (separate join/leave announcements), group-level leave only on the group's last conn, group-level send gate (member group broadcasts, non-participant group is a silent no-op). `groups.rs` pure `group_key` tests + a `#[ignore]`d live-DB test (root → self-group, subaccount → parent-group, unknown → `None`), mirroring the `db.rs` R-7 `MYSQL_URL` pattern. `ws.rs` tests: subaccount message group stamping, join outcome carrying the resolved parent, `parentAccountId` surfaced in identify success. The two existing load tests (100 conns / 1000 broadcasts / 0 drops and 100 conns / 1000 chat broadcasts / 0 drops) are updated for the group-keyed registry with mixed root/subaccount assignments.
- `tests/ws_integration.rs` — explicit `/ws` upgrade regression guard for the `Option<web::Data<MySqlPool>>` extractor (no-pool app still upgrades; existing no-pool tests also exercise this path).

### Note
- Group resolution is server-derived from the ticketed alias only (`players.id` lookup) — a client can never choose its own group. Immediate-parent one hop only (nested-subaccount roots are follow-up). Presence stays per-alias; grouping applies to channel participation only. Recorded as a `docs/memory.md` decision.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-08-25 — WebSocket chat message broadcast (task 0.3.13)

### Changed
- `src/sockets/channels.rs` — the channel hub now broadcasts chat too. A new `ChannelMessage` message (`channel_id`, ticketed sender `alias_id`, text) fans out the Talo-shaped `v1.channels.message` envelope (`channel.id`, plain-string `message`, sender `playerAlias.id`) to **every member connection, sender included** — the 0.3.10 echo shape (`{ id, from: "server", message:{…} }` with timestamp+counter message ids) is dropped in favor of the verified upstream fan-out. Membership recipients were re-typed to a single joint notification enum `ChannelNotification` (`Change(ChannelChange)` | `Message(ChannelMessage)`), so one `Recipient` per connection carries both join/leave and chat fan-outs from the same registry. The hub prunes dead recipients per broadcast, and only members may broadcast: a non-member's send — or one into an unknown/empty channel — is a silent no-op (v0 trade-off over Talo's "Player not in channel" rejection). New `channel_message_payload` envelope builder and `MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE_CHARS` (1000) cap.
- `src/sockets/ws.rs` — the routed `v1.channels.message` request is now `&self` `handle_channels_message`, gated on having identified, validating integer `channelId`, non-empty `message` ≤1000 chars; the sender alias is stamped from the socket ticket (never a body `playerAliasId` claim). `FrameOutcome` gains `BroadcastMessage(ChannelMessage)` and the stream loop dispatches it straight to the hub. `WsConn` implements `Handler<ChannelNotification>` (instead of `Handler<ChannelChange>`) rendering either envelope. `MSG_SEQ` (message-id counter) removed.

### Added
- Hub unit tests: message fans out to all members incl. sender, per-conn single delivery (one envelope per conn key), unknown-channel no-op, non-member send no-op, `channel_message_payload` shape, plus a chat load test (100 conns, 1000 chat broadcasts → 0 dropped/double-delivered envelopes). `ws.rs` unit tests: broadcast outcome with ticketed (spoof-proof) sender alias, pre-identify error, missing `channelId`/`message` errors, length cap boundary (cap-long accepted, cap+1 rejected); the same-second message-id uniqueness test is removed with the echo shape.

### Note
- `v1.channels.message` is a Playzoid **request** extension (`channelId` field, like the 0.3.12 join/leave); the response envelope is the verified Talo fan-out shape. Recorded as a `docs/memory.md` decision.

---

### Added
- `src/sockets/channels.rs` — new in-memory `ChannelHub` actix actor with `JoinChannel` / `LeaveChannel` / `LeaveAllChannels` / `ChannelChange` messages plus the `player_joined_payload` and `player_left_payload` envelope builders. A player joins a channel when its first connection registers and leaves when its last connection drops; both transitions fan out the Talo-shaped `v1.channels.player-joined` (`channel.id`, `playerAlias.id`) and `v1.channels.player-left` (`+ meta.reason` numeric 0) envelopes to member sockets. Joining an already-member alias is idempotent (no re-broadcast) and the departed connection never receives its own leave. Membership is keyed `channel → alias → conn_key`, with a reverse `conn_key → memberships` index so `LeaveAllChannels` (issued on disconnect) is O(a connection's channels), plus a per-membership cap (256 conns) pruning dead recipients. Alias ids only come from the server-resolved socket ticket — client claims are rejected. Process-global `hub()` accessor needs no `main.rs` wiring.
- `src/sockets/ws.rs` — `process_text_frame` now returns a pure `FrameOutcome` enum (`None` / `Identify` / `JoinChannel` / `LeaveChannel`) instead of a boolean, describing the *intended* hub action so the hot frame loop stays side-effect-free. New `v1.channels.join` / `v1.channels.leave` request tokens: gated on having identified first, `channelId` required (else `INVALID_INPUT`), and dispatched to the channel hub with the ticketed alias. `WsConn` implements `Handler<ChannelChange>` rendering the verified envelopes; `stopping()` additionally sends `LeaveAllChannels` beside the existing `LeavePresence`, so a dropped connection auto-leaves every channel it joined.
- Hub unit tests: first-join broadcast incl. joiner, alias-level join idempotency (second conn silent but still subscribed), multi-alias join fan-out, leave-only-on-last-conn broadcast to survivors, surviving-conn leave no-op, non-member leave no-op, disconnect leaves all channels, payload shapes (incl. numeric leave reason), plus a load test (100 conns, 1000 membership broadcasts, 0 dropped/double-delivered envelopes). `ws.rs` unit tests: join/leave success outcomes, missing `channelId` errors, pre-identify errors; existing identify tests updated to the `FrameOutcome` return.

### Note
- `v1.channels.join` / `v1.channels.leave` **request** tokens are a Playzoid extension — upstream Talo drives channel membership over HTTP and only fans the membership changes out over sockets. The response envelopes stay 100% Talo-verified. Recorded as a `docs/memory.md` decision.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-08-25 — WebSocket presence broadcast (task 0.3.11)

### Added
- `src/sockets/presence.rs` — new in-memory `PresenceHub` actix actor with `JoinPresence` / `LeavePresence` / `PresenceChange` messages plus the `presence_payload` envelope builder. A player goes `online` when its first identified connection appears and `offline` when its last connection drops; both transitions fan out the Talo-shaped `v1.players.presence.updated` envelope (`presence.playerAlias.id`, `presence.online`, `presence.lastSeenAt`, `meta.onlineChanged`) to every connected socket. Alias ids only ever come from the server-resolved socket ticket — client claims are rejected. Connections are tracked per alias by a unique `conn_key`; the disconnect path (`stopping()`) unregisters via `LeavePresence`, so offline fires exactly on the last disconnect. A per-alias cap (256 conns) prunes dead recipients to bound memory. Process-global `hub()` accessor needs no `main.rs` wiring.
- `src/sockets/ws.rs` — `WsConn` now carries a unique `conn_key` + `identified` flag; presence registration fires on `v1.players.identify` success (recipient = the connection's own address), matching Talo timing, and `stopping()` unregisters only if the connection had identified. `process_text_frame` became a `&mut self` method that also reports whether the frame armed a presence join.
- Hub unit tests: online/offline transition fan-out (including to non-transitioning subscribers being excluded), offline-only-on-last-disconnect refcounting, unsubscribe stops delivery, unknown-alias leave ignored, payload shape. `ws.rs` unit tests: identify marks the connection identified / error paths don't, presence alias comes from the resolved ticket (never a body claim), leave arm-only-when-identified.
- `tests/ws_integration.rs` — upgrade still returns 101 with a valid `?ticket=` (plus the existing no-ticket 101 and method-mismatch cases).

- `src/main.rs` — `redis::aio::ConnectionManager` initialised at startup and injected as optional app_data (caching gracefully disabled if Redis is unreachable).

## [Unreleased] — 2026-05-27 — Ralph autonomous task loop

### Added
- `AGENTS.md` — agent instruction file: required reading, branching model, code quality rules, security requirements, PR requirements, TODO status markers.
- `skills/ralph.md` — autonomous task agent skill document, adapted for the Playzoid-Server PR-based workflow (no auto-merge; opens PRs for human review).
- `scripts/ralph.sh` — POSIX shell task loop: parses `docs/TODO.md` table format, creates `task/<phase>-<num>` branches, invokes copilot, runs the three-check gate (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`) with 3-attempt retry, commits + pushes, opens PR via `gh pr create`, marks task `📬 PR #<n>` in TODO.md, and logs to `docs/ralph-log.md`. Supports `--minutes`, `--hours`, `--loop`, single-task, and graceful-stop modes.
- `scripts/ralph.ps1` — PowerShell 5.1+ port of `ralph.sh` for Windows (and pwsh anywhere).
- `tests/ralph/ralph.tests.ps1` — Pester test suite for `ralph.ps1` helper logic: 30 tests covering `Get-NextTask`, `Get-CurrentPhase`, `Get-TaskPhase`, `Get-TaskDefinitionRow`, argument parsing, task-id format validation, and `ralph.ps1` syntax.
- `docs/ralph-log.md` — append-only timestamped log for the ralph agent.
